title: Material sorting cards: wood, metal, plastic, glass, paper
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Everyday materials and how they change (Muck, Mess & Mixtures and Will It Degrade?)
source: Seeded from science/y2 lesson 5 (Material sorting cards: wood, metal, plastic, glass, paper (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 5: What are everyday materials?. To understand that everyday objects are made from different materials for a reason

blocks.title: Sort into: Wood / Metal / Plastic / Glass
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Wood, Metal, Plastic, Glass.
blocks.answer: Wood: a ruler; a chopping board. Metal: a key; a coin. Plastic: a bottle; a toy brick. Glass: a window; a jar

questions.q: What is a coin made of?
questions.model: It is hard, cold and shiny. Those are clues for metal. A coin is made of metal.

questions.q: What is a jar often made of?
Name an object made of two materials.
questions.a: For example: a pencil (wood and graphite), scissors (metal and plastic)

questions.q: Core: Material hunt in the kitchen: find one object made of each of wood, metal, plastic, glass and paper. Show each one.
questions.a: For example: wooden spoon, metal fork, plastic tub, glass jar, paper bag
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: this is a paper bag. It is thin and folds. It is paper.

questions.q: Extend: Choose one object and say why it is made of that material.
questions.a: For example: a fork is metal because metal is strong and hard

questions.q: Stretch: Name a material that is natural and one made by people.
questions.a: Natural: wood or stone; made by people: plastic or glass

questions.q: A plastic tub is made of plastic:
Big question: why are spoons not made of paper?
questions.a: Paper is weak and soaks up water, so it would tear and go soggy
